aggressiveExecution.singletonCascadeLane: One Opus or Kimi lane owns compiler, theme schema, shared roots, recipes, contracts, manifests and shared foundation tokens. It integrates requests from product slices; no second writer touches those authorities.
aggressiveExecution.preparationLaw: Sonnet scouts current and next slices in parallel. Multiple Opus writers implement disjoint source worktrees. Fable audits every integrated lot. Codex audits each integrated slice and any compiler, manifest, public-control or hard-to-reverse architecture change. Heavy build, server and browser work runs once per integrated batch.
aggressiveExecution.toolingLaw: Freeze new Modern Rescue scripts. The existing manifest generator is not yet source-derived: extend packages/core/scripts/generate/tokens/manifest/generation/index.mjs itself so declared target edges, observed compiler/CSS edges and gaps are generated and productive sources enter freshness. Run it once per integrated batch. A non-blocking Sonnet lane audits all packages/core/scripts and migrates it in mechanical batches to domain/subdomain/capability/index: related behavior is grouped, opaque historical or agent names are retired, callers are updated with tests, duplicates and dead entrypoints are removed. It also rehomes test artifacts by purpose after complete reference/digest inventory. It starts with root exceptions, recursive tests, non-consumable materialize/backlog producers and duplicate CSS census after unique facts migrate; it may not design another platform or consume the product-source budget.
aggressiveExecution.autonomy: A correction inside the authorized scope is remediated immediately after source-grounded Fable/Codex review. Do not wait for the owner except for product/commercial scope, incompatible public API, destructive or external action, release, publish or push.

A domain that must not be written in the round is declared no-write WITH A REASON; leaving it implicit is the defect this registry exists to prevent.
